title: This Shoe Company’s Instagram Ad With a Frat Is Pissing People Off
gist: HeyDude, the Crocs-owned shoe brand, drew boycott calls after a September 25 Instagram post with University of Florida Theta Chi, whose two former members face charges over distributing a nonconsensual intimate video. HeyDude says the post was part of a 'Tailgate Tour' and it was unaware of the allegations, and says it will reevaluate stops, but the post remained up.

insights.claim: HeyDude, acquired by Crocs in 2022, posted on Instagram and TikTok with UF Theta Chi on September 25, 2026, triggering #CancelHeyDude backlash because two former chapter members face nonconsensual-image charges.
insights.speaker: Ej Dickson
insights.so_what: Influencer-style campus marketing creates brand-safety risk for Crocs' fast-growing HeyDude unit.

insights.claim: HeyDude says it had no affiliation, sponsorship or ongoing partnership with the chapter, that the post was part of a nationwide 'Tailgate Tour' including frat and sorority houses, and that it was unaware of the allegations when planning, and will reevaluate remaining stops.
insights.speaker: HeyDude spokesperson
insights.so_what: Greek-life activation tours lack vetting and expose consumer brands to reputational contagion.
insights.quote: We will reevaluate future stops for the remainder of the tour.
insights.locator: In a statement to WIRED, a HeyDude spokesperson

insights.claim: Despite the backlash and the company's statement, the HeyDude post was still live as of Friday morning, and the Kowalskis' emails to the company went unanswered.
insights.speaker: Ej Dickson
insights.so_what: Slow crisis response lets a social-media controversy persist and amplifies consumer-boycott risk.
insights.quote: As of Friday morning, the post was still up.

insights.claim: Activist @bluraybeyond argues HeyDude's collaboration rewards sexual exploitation with 'free PR swag' and echoes institutional indifference seen at Cornell and the DA's office.
insights.speaker: Ej Dickson
insights.so_what: Creator-activist amplification is the vehicle by which brand controversies spread among Gen Z consumers.

insights.claim: Two former UF Theta Chi members allegedly used anonymous burner accounts on X to spread a nonconsensual intimate video of a 19-year-old student and named her, and are charged with sexual cyberharassment, a first-degree misdemeanor carrying up to a year in jail and a $1,000 fine.
insights.speaker: Ej Dickson
insights.so_what: Platform anonymity and viral reach remain a liability and enforcement gap for social platforms like X.

insights.claim: The victim is also suing both men for damages in Florida Northern District Court, and the affidavit says posts accumulated thousands of views and went viral.
insights.speaker: Ej Dickson
insights.so_what: Civil suits add financial exposure beyond misdemeanour penalties for individuals who weaponise social media.

insights.so_what: Meme-coin tooling is being used for harassment, a reputational overhang for crypto launchpads.

insights.claim: Theta Chi has more than 246 chapters and 250,000 initiated members, with 190 active members at UF, and says it would support maximum penalties and permanent expulsion if guilt is determined.
insights.speaker: Theta Chi representative
insights.so_what: Scale of national fraternities makes them targets for reputation campaigns and partnership scrutiny.

insights.claim: The Cornell Sun's mid-September publication of names of seven students accused of a 2024 gang rape at a Chi Phi house sparked broad social-media criticism of frat culture, heightening scrutiny of brand partnerships.
insights.speaker: Ej Dickson
insights.so_what: Concurrent campus scandals raise reputational risk for any brand marketing to fraternities.
